newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-BHP SHUTS OK TEDI MILL DUE TO DRY.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-BHP SHUTS OK TEDI MILL DUE TO DRY.

text.p: The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd said on Tuesday that it had shut the mill at the Ok Tedi copper and gold mine in Papua New Guinea due to dry weather conditions.
BHP said further dry conditions has caused water levels in the Fly River to fall, and interrupted river navigation.
River vessels are used by the company to transport copper concentrate to the silo vessel MV Karbi and to back load essential supplies, BHP said.
"In view of low inventories of diesel fuel, management has decided to shut down mill operations and bring forward maintenance work. Operations in the mine are continuing," BHP said.
BHP said a copper concentrate vessel departed from the MV Karabi last week.
Further shipments will be postponed until the Fly River is again navigable, and copper concentrate stocks on the Karabi can be replenished.
Ok Tedi Mining Ltd was forced to suspend concentrate barge traffic down the Fly for most of June owing to lowe river levels.

Ok Tedi has long-term supply contracts with Germany's Norddeutsche Affinerie, Finland's Outokumpu Oy, Philippines Associated Smelting and Refining Corp (PASAR), South Korea's LG Metals Corp, Mitsui & Co Ltd and the Japanese Smelter Pool which consists of seven Japanese smelters.
BHP owns 52.6 percent of the mine. The other partners are Canada's Inmet Mining Corp with 17.4 percent and the PNG government, which holds the rest.
